findings.problem: BatchWorkflow uses a String for status instead of a domain enum, allowing any string value including invalid lifecycle transitions
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set status to any string (e.g., "deleted", "", "SENT") making illegal states representable and bypassing lifecycle invariants
findings.fix: Replace with a sealed BatchStatus enum: pub enum BatchStatus { Draft, Validated, Sent } and expose only a &self accessor

findings.problem: Lifecycle state is modeled as a boolean field instead of a typestate transition, allowing contradictory states like is_validated=false with is_sent=true
findings.failure_mode: Caller can set is_sent=true while is_validated=false, producing a logically impossible batch state that silently violates the validation-before-sent invariant
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single typestate enum: pub enum BatchState { Draft, Validated { sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> }, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }

findings.problem: Lifecycle boolean that can be set independently of status string and is_validated boolean, creating unenforceable state machine
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent sets is_sent=true and status="sent" but does not touch is_validated, so a BatchWorkflow{is_validated:false, is_sent:true, status:"sent"} is constructible and semantically invalid
findings.fix: Fold lifecycle into typestate enum so sent state variant owns the sent_at_epoch_ms field and the transition enforces prior validation

findings.problem: Optional lifecycle timestamp is a bare field that can be None even when is_sent=true, or Some when is_sent=false, with no coupling to the lifecycle state
findings.failure_mode: BatchWorkflow{is_sent:true, sent_at_epoch_ms:None} is representable, losing the sent timestamp invariant; conversely BatchWorkflow{is_sent:false, sent_at_epoch_ms:Some(123)} leaks future state
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the typestate variant that owns it, e.g. Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } with no Option

findings.problem: BatchWorkflow uses raw String for id and has no smart constructor, so raw primitives cross the parse boundary without validation; callers can construct invalid domain states directly
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can instantiate BatchWorkflow with an empty string, null-like content, or unbounded id, bypassing domain validation at construction time
findings.fix: Add a BatchId newtype with a smart constructor returning a typed error, and make BatchWorkflow private with a smart constructor that validates all invariants

findings.problem: Struct has all public fields with no constructor, no validation, and no encapsulation — illegal states are fully representable
findings.failure_mode: Callers bypass all invariants by direct field mutation or by constructing the struct with arbitrary values, making the type contract unenforceable
findings.fix: Make struct private, add a newtype/enum typestate for lifecycle, and provide a single BatchWorkflow::new(...) -> Result<Self, BatchError> smart constructor

findings.construct: pub fn mark_sent(mut item: BatchWorkflow) -> BatchWorkflow
findings.problem: mark_sent does not check is_validated before marking sent, and mutates status string directly — no precondition enforcement, no typed return
findings.failure_mode: A Draft batch (is_validated=false) can be transitively sent by calling mark_sent, silently producing an invalid lifecycle transition with no error returned
findings.fix: Return Result<BatchWorkflow, BatchError::NotValidated>; check typestate variant before allowing Sent transition; remove mutable struct — return a new instance

findings.problem: String allocation via .to_string() on a literal in the domain struct mutation indicates domain logic is doing string construction instead of using enum variants
findings.failure_mode: Allocation happens inside the domain layer instead of the shell; every call allocates even when the value is a constant, and the domain exposes string internals
findings.fix: Replace String status with enum variant; eliminate .to_string() on domain data

findings.construct: pub fn mark_sent(mut item: BatchWorkflow) -> BatchWorkflow
findings.problem: mark_sent takes and returns the struct by value with no Result type, so there is no error taxonomy for invalid transitions
findings.failure_mode: Invalid lifecycle transitions are silently accepted rather than returned as typed errors, preventing callers from handling failure cases explicitly
findings.fix: Change signature to pub fn mark_sent(item: BatchWorkflow) -> Result<BatchWorkflow, BatchError>

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for any performance-relevant code path
findings.failure_mode: Performance claims about mark_sent or BatchWorkflow cannot be verified; hidden allocations from String to_string() are unmeasured
findings.fix: Add a criterion or simple benchmark measuring allocation profile of mark_sent across state transitions

findings.problem: No test module exists; no cargo test, clippy, or fmt evidence for review
findings.failure_mode: No behavioral evidence exists to validate that the review findings are correct or that fixes would compile
findings.fix: Add a test module with invalid-state construction attempts, typestate transition tests, and smart constructor validation tests

findings.problem: All struct fields are public, allowing direct mutation without any domain invariants or typestate enforcement
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can mutate id, status, is_validated, is_sent, or sent_at_epoch_ms independently, producing inconsistent state without the struct's knowledge
findings.fix: Make fields private; expose immutable borrows via getters; mutate only through typed methods or smart constructors

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or BatchWorkflow allocation profile
no profiler evidence for String allocation hotspots
no allocation measurement (e.g., heaptrack or criterion) for mark_sent
no second-ring command evidence (cargo clippy / cargo test) run against the crate
no command-truth evidence that fixes would compile and pass tests
residual_risk: Static review only. The crate has no tests, no benchmarks, and no command evidence. All findings are structural violations of Holzman Rust absolute laws: status String, lifecycle booleans, bare Option, no smart constructor, no typed errors, no typestate. The type BatchWorkflow is fully reversible to valid/invalid states by any caller. Fix requires refactoring to a sealed typestate enum, newtyped domain IDs, a Result-returning mark_sent, and a private struct with smart constructor.
